locus: Theses in quibus exponitur Doctrina Scholae Romanae circa partitionem Gratiae in sufficientem atque efficacem, & concordiam libertatis humanae cum Gratiae efficacia, CVIII-CXV (the print has no CXIII) (the recent Thomists (Alvarez) and Molina diametrically opposed: on how grace works, efficacious of itself against efficacy from consent; on what grace is, a virtual motion against natural affections of the will made supernatural; Jansenius with the Thomists on the first point but nearer Molina on the second, placing efficacious grace in vital affections of love and desire, heavenly delight; he differs from Molina in having them sent wholly from heaven, not arising naturally; Molina makes a natural affection precede every free act, even the first sins of man and angel (Genesis 3:6), Jansenius denies it of the will as such and of the first sin).
